A FEW WAYS IN

About this experiment

DRAG SETS LOWER ANGLE · ARROWS SET ANGLES · SPACE REPLAYS · P PAUSES

The mathematics

Two equal point masses hang from rigid, massless rods of equal length. Angles are measured from the downward vertical; each slider sets a starting angle and releases both masses from rest. The brighter rods show the main pendulum; the faint twin starts with its lower angle just 0.01° larger. At energetic starting positions their paths can diverge. Small oscillations can remain regular. There is no damping or forcing. Eight fourth-order Runge–Kutta substeps per display tick approximate the equations; the energy drift readout reports numerical error. Space resets the same release, R cycles starting positions, and P pauses. Drag sets the lower starting angle. Trails retain the latest 30 seconds.
